questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 12 days. What fraction of the work does A complete in one day?
questions.explanation: If A completes the work in 12 days, A's one-day work = 1/12.

questions.question: A can complete a work in 10 days and B can complete the same work in 15 days. How many days will they take to complete it together?
questions.explanation: Combined one-day work = 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6. Therefore, they complete the work in 6 days.

questions.question: A can complete a work in 12 days and B can complete it in 18 days. What is the efficiency ratio of A to B?
questions.explanation: Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. Therefore, efficiency ratio A:B = 18:12 = 3:2.

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 8 days. A alone can complete it in 12 days. How many days will B alone take?
questions.explanation: B's one-day work = 1/8 − 1/12 = 3/24 − 2/24 = 1/24. Therefore, B alone takes 24 days.

questions.question: A can complete a work in 20 days. What fraction of the work remains after A works for 8 days?
questions.explanation: Work completed in 8 days = 8/20 = 2/5. Remaining work = 1 − 2/5 = 3/5.

questions.question: A can complete a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. A works alone for 4 days, after which B joins. How much more time will they take to finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation: A completes 4/12 = 1/3 of the work. Remaining work = 2/3. Their combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36. Time required = (2/3) ÷ (5/36) = 24/5 = 4.8 days.

questions.question: 12 workers can complete a task in 15 days. How many days will 20 workers take to complete the same task, assuming equal efficiency?
questions.explanation: For the same work, workers × days remains constant. Therefore, 12 × 15 = 20 × D. D = 180/20 = 9 days.

questions.question: A and B have efficiencies in the ratio 3:2. If they receive $500 for completing a work together, how much should A receive?
questions.explanation: Wages are divided according to work efficiency. A's share = 3/(3 + 2) × $500 = 3/5 × $500 = $300.

questions.question: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours and a leak empties the full tank in 24 hours. How long will the tank take to fill when both operate together?
questions.explanation: Net filling rate = 1/8 − 1/24 = 3/24 − 1/24 = 2/24 = 1/12. Therefore, the tank fills in 12 hours.

questions.question: A is 25% more efficient than B. If B completes a work in 20 days, how many days will A take?
questions.explanation: If B's efficiency is 100, A's efficiency is 125. Their efficiency ratio is 5:4, so their time ratio is 4:5. A's time = 20 × 4/5 = 16 days.
